items.stem: Complete the statement: When a limited company buys an unincorporated business, the assets acquired are recorded in the company's books at …
options: the seller's book values
their replacement cost in five years
their fair values at the date of acquisition
their original cost
items.answer: their fair values at the date of acquisition
items.markingKey: IFRS 3: identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value [1].

items.stem: Explain why a company may prefer to pay for an acquisition with shares rather than cash.
items.answer: It conserves cash/liquidity, avoids borrowing and interest, and keeps the seller involved; but it dilutes existing shareholders' control and EPS.
items.markingKey: Liquidity/no borrowing [1]; seller shares risk [1]; drawback dilution [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why the net assets of the business bought are revalued to fair value before calculating goodwill.
items.answer: Book values may be out of date; the buyer is paying for current values, so goodwill must be measured against fair values to show the true premium paid.
items.markingKey: Book values not current [1]; goodwill = consideration − fair value [1] [2]

items.stem: Tamarind Ltd buys the business of Samuel, a sole trader in Colombo. Samuel's statement of financial position shows: premises $238,000, equipment $45,000, inventory $31,500, trade receivables $19,500, bank $9,000, trade payables $11,500. Tamarind Ltd takes over all assets except the bank account, and all liabilities. It values premises at $302,000, equipment at $42,500, inventory at $30,000 and creates an allowance of 2% for irrecoverable debts. Calculate the fair value of the net assets acquired.
items.markingKey: Premises $302,000 + equipment $42,500 + inventory $30,000 + receivables $19,500 − 2% = $19,110 [2]; − payables $11,500 [1]; fair value of net assets $382,110 [1]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: Purchase consideration is … (b) Complete the statement: When a limited company buys an unincorporated business, the assets acquired are recorded in the company's books at …
items.answer: (a) the total value of cash, shares and other securities given to the seller (b) their fair values at the date of acquisition
items.markingKey: (a) Consideration = cash + shares (at issue price) + debentures etc. [1]. (b) IFRS 3: identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value [1].

items.stem: Explain two factors a company should consider before buying an existing business.
items.answer: Profitability and future cash flows; quality of assets and liabilities taken over; price compared with value; financing method; staff and customer retention; synergies.

items.stem: When Monarch plc bought the business of Omar, the accountant recorded premises at Omar's book value of $96,000 instead of the agreed fair value of $132,000. Explain the error and its effect on goodwill and on the statement of financial position.

items.markingKey: Fair value required [1]; premises understated $36,000 [1]; goodwill overstated $36,000, total unchanged [1] [3]

items.stem: Complete the statement: Goodwill on acquisition is calculated as …
options: total assets acquired less cash paid
purchase consideration less the fair value of net assets acquired
fair value of net assets less purchase consideration
purchase consideration less book value of the seller's capital
items.answer: purchase consideration less the fair value of net assets acquired

items.stem: Explain why a buyer might pay more than the fair value of the net assets of a business.
items.answer: To obtain its goodwill: reputation, customer base, skilled staff, location, synergies and future super profits that are not recorded as separate assets.

items.stem: Explain why a seller might accept less than the fair value of its net assets.
items.answer: The seller may need to sell quickly (forced sale, retirement, financial difficulty) or the business may be making losses, so the assets will not earn a normal return.

items.stem: Sirocco plc paid $472,000 for net assets with a fair value of $502,000. The finance director wants to show the difference as "negative goodwill" deducted from intangible assets. Explain the correct treatment.
items.answer: Under IFRS 3 the fair values must first be reassessed; any remaining excess of $30,000 is a gain on bargain purchase recognised immediately in profit or loss.
items.markingKey: Reassess fair values [1]; gain on bargain purchase $30,000 [1]; to profit or loss, not intangible assets [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to the owners of two small businesses of merging into one limited company.
items.answer: Economies of scale; combined skills and resources; larger capital base and easier finance; limited liability; reduced competition.

items.stem: Explain why goodwill is often valued separately for each business before a merger.
items.answer: So that owners whose business has greater earning power receive more shares; without it, shares would reflect only tangible net assets and be unfair.
items.markingKey: Fair allocation of shares [1]; reflects earning power [1] [2]

items.stem: Odyssey plc buys the business of Mei, a sole trader in Muscat. Mei's statement of financial position shows: premises $131,000, equipment $74,000, inventory $31,500, trade receivables $19,000, bank $10,000, trade payables $22,000. Odyssey plc takes over all assets except the bank account, and all liabilities. It values premises at $155,000, equipment at $71,500, inventory at $29,000 and creates an allowance of 2% for irrecoverable debts. Calculate the fair value of the net assets acquired.
items.markingKey: Premises $155,000 + equipment $71,500 + inventory $29,000 + receivables $19,000 − 2% = $18,620 [2]; − payables $22,000 [1]; fair value of net assets $252,120 [1]

items.stem: Equinox plc buys the business of Ethan, a sole trader in Muscat. Ethan's statement of financial position shows: premises $268,000, equipment $24,000, inventory $40,500, trade receivables $16,000, bank $4,500, trade payables $11,500. Equinox plc takes over all assets except the bank account, and all liabilities. It values premises at $282,000, equipment at $19,500, inventory at $36,500 and creates an allowance of 4% for irrecoverable debts. Calculate the fair value of the net assets acquired.
items.markingKey: Premises $282,000 + equipment $19,500 + inventory $36,500 + receivables $16,000 − 4% = $15,360 [2]; − payables $11,500 [1]; fair value of net assets $341,860 [1]

items.stem: Equinox plc acquires the partnership of Chloe and Leila on 1 July. The partnership's assets and liabilities taken over, at agreed fair values, are: premises $307,000, equipment $68,500, inventory $10,500, trade receivables $21,560, trade payables $24,000. The consideration is 190,000 ordinary shares of $1 at $1.25 each, $10,000 in cash and $20,000 6% debentures at par. Before the purchase Equinox plc had ordinary share capital $600,000, share premium $29,000 and a bank balance of $173,000. (a) Calculate the purchase consideration. (b) Evaluate whether Equinox plc has paid a fair price for the business.
items.answer: (a) $267,500 (b) Goodwill of -$116,060 is -43.4% of consideration; justified only if future profits/synergies exceed the premium; consider customer loyalty, staff, risk.
items.markingKey: (a) 190,000 × $1.25 = $237,500 + $10,000 + $20,000 = $267,500 [2] (b) Uses goodwill figure [1]; future profits/synergies [1]; risks [1]; conclusion [1] [4]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: Goodwill on acquisition is calculated as … (b) Complete the statement: A gain on a bargain purchase arises when …
items.answer: (a) purchase consideration less the fair value of net assets acquired (b) the fair value of net assets acquired exceeds the purchase consideration
items.markingKey: (a) IFRS 3 [1]. (b) Negative goodwill → gain recognised in profit after reassessment [1].

items.stem: Cobalt Ltd paid $227,000 for net assets with a fair value of $238,000. The finance director wants to show the difference as "negative goodwill" deducted from intangible assets. Explain the correct treatment.
items.answer: Under IFRS 3 the fair values must first be reassessed; any remaining excess of $11,000 is a gain on bargain purchase recognised immediately in profit or loss.
items.markingKey: Reassess fair values [1]; gain on bargain purchase $11,000 [1]; to profit or loss, not intangible assets [1] [3]

items.stem: Ibis plc agreed to pay $489,000 for a business whose net assets have a fair value of $425,000. It pays $10,000 in cash and the balance by issuing ordinary shares of $1 at $1.25 each. Calculate the goodwill, the number of shares issued and the share premium created.
items.answer: Goodwill $64,000; 383,200 shares; share premium $95,800

items.stem: Banyan Ltd acquires Lotus Retail from Mateo. The fair value of the net assets acquired is $425,000. The consideration is 140,000 ordinary shares of $1 at $2.40 each, $37,000 in cash and $80,000 7% debentures. Calculate the purchase consideration and the goodwill or gain on bargain purchase.
items.answer: Consideration $453,000; goodwill $28,000

items.stem: Kestrel plc acquires the partnership of Diego and Noah on 1 July. The partnership's assets and liabilities taken over, at agreed fair values, are: premises $327,000, equipment $65,500, inventory $13,500, trade receivables $9,310, trade payables $16,500. The consideration is 170,000 ordinary shares of $1 at $1.25 each, $12,000 in cash and $50,000 6% debentures at par. Before the purchase Kestrel plc had ordinary share capital $550,000, share premium $32,000 and a bank balance of $283,000. (a) Calculate the purchase consideration. (b) Calculate the balances on Kestrel plc's share capital, share premium and bank accounts after the acquisition.
items.answer: (a) $274,500 (b) Share capital $720,000; share premium $74,500; bank $271,000

items.stem: Freya's business (valued at $200,000) and Kenji's business (valued at $100,000) merged. The adviser proposed issuing 150,000 shares of $1 to each owner. Explain why this may be unfair and calculate a fair allocation.
items.answer: Shares should reflect the value each owner contributes: Freya 200,000 shares, Kenji 100,000 shares. Equal allocation transfers value from the owner of the larger business.

items.stem: Jonas's business (valued at $240,000) and Tomás's business (valued at $130,000) merged. The adviser proposed issuing 185,000 shares of $1 to each owner. Explain why this may be unfair and calculate a fair allocation.
items.answer: Shares should reflect the value each owner contributes: Jonas 240,000 shares, Tomás 130,000 shares. Equal allocation transfers value from the owner of the larger business.

items.stem: Hana (sole trader, net assets $158,000) and Mei (sole trader, net assets $241,000) merge their businesses to form Meridian Ltd. Each receives ordinary shares of $1 in Meridian Ltd at par equal in value to the business contributed. Calculate the number of shares issued to each owner.
